sentences.zh: 韋臯，字城武，京兆人。

translations.literal: Wei Gao—Wei Gao, courtesy name Chengwu, was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao, whose courtesy name was Chengwu, came from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，以建陵挽郎調補華州參軍，累授使府監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era, on the basis of his service as a Jianling pallbearer he was transferred to fill the post of Huazhou assistant administrator, and was repeatedly appointed surveillance commissioner in the military governor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali reign, after serving as a pallbearer at Jianling, he was assigned as an aide in Huazhou and gradually rose to become a surveillance commissioner on his patron's staff.

sentences.zh: 宰相張鎰出為鳳翊隴右節度使，奏臯為營田判官，得殿中侍御史，權知隴州行營留後事，

translations.literal: When the chief minister Zhang Yin went out as military governor of Fengyi and Longyou, he memorialized to appoint Gao as agricultural colony adjutant; Gao received the post of attendant censor in the palace and was temporarily put in charge of the Longzhou field headquarters as acting rear-base commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yin left the capital to take command of Fengyi and Longyou, he recommended Gao as his agricultural commissioner. Gao also received appointment as an imperial attendant censor and was made acting rear-base commander at the Longzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 涇師犯闕，德宗幸奉天，鳳翔兵馬使李楚琳殺張鎰，以府城叛歸於硃泚，隴州刺史郝通奔於楚琳。

translations.literal: The Jingzhou troops assaulted the imperial precincts, and Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian; the Fengxiang troop marshal Li Chuolin killed Zhang Yin and rebelled with the prefectural city in submission to Zhu Ci, and the Longzhou prefect Hao Tong fled to Chuolin.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers from Jing rebelled and marched on the capital, forcing Emperor Dezong to take refuge at Fengtian. Li Chuolin, the Fengxiang troop commander, killed Zhang Yin and surrendered the city to Zhu Ci, while Longzhou's prefect Hao Tong defected to Chuolin.

sentences.zh: 先是，硃泚自范陽入朝，以甲士自隨；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhu Ci had come to court from Fanyang, he had brought armored soldiers with him;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhu Ci had come to court from Fanyang, he had brought armored troops with him;

sentences.zh: 後泚為鳳翔節度使，既罷，留范陽五百人戍隴州，而泚舊將牛雲光督之。

translations.literal: later, when Ci served as military governor of Fengxiang and then left the post, he left five hundred men from Fanyang to garrison Longzhou, under the supervision of his former general Niu Yunguang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Zhu Ci had served as military governor of Fengxiang and left that post, he left five hundred Fanyang troops to garrison Longzhou under his former general Niu Yunguang.

sentences.zh: 時泚既以逆徒圍奉天，雲光因稱疾，請臯為帥，將謀亂，擒臯以赴泚。

translations.literal: At that time Ci had already had his rebel forces besiege Fengtian; Yunguang feigned illness and asked that Gao be made commander, intending to plot rebellion and seize Gao to deliver him to Ci.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhu Ci's rebels were besieging Fengtian. Yunguang pretended to be ill and proposed making Gao commander, planning a mutiny that would seize Gao and hand him over to Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 臯將翟曄伺知之，白臯為備；

translations.literal: Gao's officer Zhai Ye detected this and informed Gao to take precautions;
translations.idiomatic: Gao's officer Zhai Ye discovered the plot and warned Gao to prepare;

sentences.zh: 雲光知事泄，遂率其兵以奔泚。

translations.literal: when Yunguang learned that the affair had leaked out, he led his troops in flight to join Ci.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunguang learned the plot had been exposed, he led his troops away to join Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 行及汧陽，遇泚家僮蘇玉將使於臯所，蘇玉謂雲光曰：「太尉已登寶位，使我持詔以韋臯為御史中丞，君可以兵歸隴州。

translations.literal: When he reached Qianyang, he met Ci's household slave Su Yu, who was being sent as envoy to Gao's post; Su Yu said to Yunguang, "The Grand Preceptor has already ascended the throne and has sent me with an edict appointing Wei Gao as vice censor-in-chief. You may return your troops to Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the road at Qianyang he met Zhu Ci's household slave Su Yu, who was on his way to Gao with a message. Su Yu told Yunguang, "The Grand Preceptor has already taken the throne and has sent me with an edict making Wei Gao vice censor-in-chief. You can take your troops back to Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 臯若承命，即為吾人；

translations.literal: If Gao accepts the command, he will be one of us;
translations.idiomatic: If Gao accepts the order, he will be on our side;

sentences.zh: 如不受詔，彼書生，可以圖之，事無不濟矣。」

translations.literal: if he does not accept the edict, he is only a scholar—you can deal with him, and the affair cannot fail to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: if he refuses the edict, he is only a scholar—you can take him, and the plan cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 乃反昪疾趨隴州。

translations.literal: Then they turned back and, feigning illness, hurried on to Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They then turned back and, pretending illness, pressed on toward Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 臯迎勞之，先納蘇玉，受其偽命，乃問雲光曰：「始不告而去，今又來，何也？」

translations.literal: Gao went out to welcome and console them; he first received Su Yu and accepted the false appointment, then asked Yunguang, "At first you left without telling me; now you have come again—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao went out to welcome them. He first admitted Su Yu and accepted the bogus appointment, then asked Yunguang, "You left without a word before—why have you come back now?"

sentences.zh: 雲光曰：「前未知公心，故潛去；

translations.literal: Yunguang said, "Before, I did not know your mind, so I slipped away secretly;
translations.idiomatic: Yunguang said, "Before, I did not know where you stood, so I left in secret;

sentences.zh: 知公有新命，今乃復還。

translations.literal: now that I know you have received a new appointment, I have returned.
translations.idiomatic: now that I know you have a new commission, I have come back.

sentences.zh: 願與公戮力定功，同其生死。」

translations.literal: I wish to join my strength with yours to establish merit and share life and death alike."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to join forces with you to win glory and share life and death."

sentences.zh: 臯曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Gao said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "Very well."

sentences.zh: 又謂雲光曰：「大使茍不懷詐，請納器甲，使城中無所危疑，乃可入。」

translations.literal: He also said to Yunguang, "If the envoy truly harbors no treachery, please hand over weapons and armor so that the city will have no cause for alarm or suspicion; only then may you enter."
translations.idiomatic: He added to Yunguang, "If you truly mean no treachery, surrender your weapons and armor so the city will have no reason to fear you—only then may you enter."

sentences.zh: 雲光以書生待臯，且以為信然，乃盡付弓矢戈甲。

translations.literal: Yunguang, treating Gao as a mere scholar and believing him sincere, handed over all his bows, arrows, spears, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Taking Gao for a mere scholar and believing him, Yunguang surrendered all his bows, arrows, spears, and armor.

sentences.zh: 臯既受之，乃內其兵。

translations.literal: Once Gao had received them, he admitted the troops within the walls.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao took possession of the arms, he let the troops inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 明日，臯犒宴蘇玉、雲光之卒於郡舍，伏甲於兩廊。

translations.literal: The next day Gao feasted Su Yu and Yunguang's soldiers at the prefectural residence, with armored men concealed in both corridors.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Gao entertained Su Yu and Yunguang's men at the prefectural hall, with armed men hidden in both corridors.

sentences.zh: 酒既行，伏發，盡誅之，斬雲光、蘇玉首以徇。

translations.literal: When the wine had been served, the ambush was sprung and all were slaughtered; the heads of Yunguang and Su Yu were cut off and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the wine was flowing, the ambush struck and all were killed. The heads of Yunguang and Su Yu were cut off and displayed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 泚又使家僮劉海廣以臯為鳳翔節度使，臯斬海廣及從者三人，生一人，使報泚。

translations.literal: Ci again sent his household slave Liu Haiguang to appoint Gao military governor of Fengxiang; Gao beheaded Haiguang and three attendants, spared one man, and sent him to report to Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci again sent his slave Liu Haiguang to offer Gao the Fengxiang command. Gao executed Haiguang and three of his escorts, spared one man, and sent him back to Zhu Ci with the news.

sentences.zh: 於是詔以臯為御史大夫、隴州刺史，置奉義軍節度以旌之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict appointed Gao censor-in-chief and prefect of Longzhou, and established the Fengyi Army command as a mark of honor for him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then appointed Gao censor-in-chief and prefect of Longzhou and created the Fengyi Army command to honor his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 臯遣從兄平及弇繼入奉天城，城中聞臯有備，士氣增倍。

translations.literal: Gao sent his cousin Ping and Yan Ji into Fengtian city; when the city heard that Gao was prepared, morale doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent his cousin Ping and Yan Ji into Fengtian. When the besieged city learned that Gao was secure, morale soared.

sentences.zh: 臯乃築壇於廷，血牲與將士等盟曰：「上天不吊，國家多難，逆臣乘間，盜據宮闈。

translations.literal: Gao then built an altar in the courtyard, sacrificed a bloody victim, and with the generals and soldiers swore an oath, saying, "Heaven does not pity us; the state faces many calamities; rebel ministers seize their chance and steal possession of the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Gao built an altar in the courtyard, offered a blood sacrifice, and swore an oath with his officers and men: "Heaven has turned away; the realm is beset with troubles. Traitors have seized their moment and seized the palace.

sentences.zh: 而李楚琳亦扇兇徒，傾陷城邑，酷虐所加，爰及本使，既不事上，安能恤下。

translations.literal: Li Chuolin too has incited violent men and overthrown cities; the cruelty he inflicts reaches even to this commissioner. Since he will not serve his sovereign, how can he care for his subordinates?
translations.idiomatic: Li Chuolin too has stirred up ruffians and overrun cities. His cruelty has reached even to our commissioner. A man who will not serve his sovereign cannot care for his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 臯是用激心憤氣，不遑底寧，誓與群公，竭誠王室。

translations.literal: For this reason Gao's heart is stirred and his anger aroused; he has no leisure for repose and swears with you all to devote his utmost loyalty to the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason my heart burns and my anger will not rest. I swear with you all to give our full loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 凡我同盟，一心協力，仗順除兇，先祖之靈，必當幽贊。

translations.literal: All who are allied with me—unite your hearts and join your strength; relying on righteousness, destroy the wicked; the spirits of our forefathers will surely aid us from the unseen realm.
translations.idiomatic: Let all who stand with me unite in one purpose and, upholding the righteous cause, destroy these villains. The spirits of our ancestors will surely aid us.

sentences.zh: 言誠則誌合，義感則心齊；

translations.literal: when words are sincere, wills align; when righteousness moves us, hearts unite;
translations.idiomatic: When speech is sincere, purpose aligns; when righteousness moves us, hearts unite;

sentences.zh: 粉骨糜軀，決無所顧。

translations.literal: to grind our bones to powder and waste our bodies—we will never hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: though our bones be ground to dust and our bodies destroyed, we shall not flinch.

sentences.zh: 有渝此誌，明神殛之，迨於子孫，亦罔遺類。

translations.literal: Whoever violates this oath, may the bright spirits strike him down, even unto his descendants, leaving none behind.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever breaks this oath, may the spirits strike him down, even to his descendants, leaving not one survivor.

sentences.zh: 皇天後土，當兆斯言。」

translations.literal: May Heaven above and Earth below bear witness to these words."
translations.idiomatic: May Heaven and Earth bear witness to these words."

sentences.zh: 又遣使入吐蕃求援。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys into Tibet to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to Tibet to request assistance.

sentences.zh: 十一月，加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was additionally appointed acting minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he received the additional title of acting minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，德宗還京，征為左金吾衛將軍，尋遷大將軍，

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, when Dezong returned to the capital, Gao was summoned as general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and soon promoted to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan, after Dezong returned to the capital, Gao was recalled as general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and soon promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，拜檢校戶部尚書，兼成都尹、御史大夫、劍南西川節度使，代張延賞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, He was appointed acting minister of revenue, concurrently prefect of Chengdu, censor-in-chief, and military governor of Jiannan West Circuit, replacing Zhang Yanshang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan, He was appointed acting minister of revenue, concurrently made prefect of Chengdu, censor-in-chief, and military governor of western Jiannan, replacing Zhang Yanshang.

sentences.zh: 臯以雲南蠻眾數十萬，與吐蕃和好，蕃人入寇，必以蠻為前鋒。

translations.literal: Gao observed that the Yunnan barbarians numbered several hundred thousand, were on friendly terms with Tibet, and whenever Tibetans invaded, they invariably used the barbarians as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Gao saw that the Yunnan tribes numbered hundreds of thousands, were allied with Tibet, and whenever Tibetans raided, they always used the tribesmen as their vanguard.

sentences.zh: 四年，臯遣判官崔佐時入南詔蠻，說令向化，以離吐蕃之助。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Gao sent his adjutant Cui Zuoshi into the Nanzhao barbarians to persuade them to turn toward civilization and thereby sever Tibet's support.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Gao sent his adjutant Cui Zuoshi into Nanzhao to persuade the tribes to submit to the court and thus break Tibet's alliance with them.

sentences.zh: 佐時至蠻國羊咀咩城，其王異牟尋忻然接遇，請絕吐蕃，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Zuoshi reached the barbarian capital of Yangjumie; their king Yimouxun received him gladly, asked to break with Tibet, and sent envoys to offer tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: Zuoshi reached the tribal capital at Yangjumie. King Yimouxun welcomed him gladly, asked to sever ties with Tibet, and sent envoys to pay tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 其年，遣東蠻鬼主驃傍、苴夢沖、苴烏等相率入朝。

translations.literal: That year the eastern barbarian spirit-lords Piaobang, Jumengchong, Juwu, and others led their people in succession to court.
translations.idiomatic: That year the eastern tribal spirit-lords Piaobang, Jumengchong, Juwu, and others led delegations to the capital.

sentences.zh: 南蠻自巂州陷沒，臣屬吐蕃，絕朝貢者二十余年，至是復通。

translations.literal: The southern barbarians, since the fall of Xi Prefecture, had submitted to Tibet and had broken off tribute to the court for more than twenty years; now contact was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xi Prefecture had fallen, the southern tribes had submitted to Tibet and ceased tribute for more than twenty years; now relations were restored.

sentences.zh: 五年，臯遣大將王有道簡習精卒以入蕃界，與東蠻於故巂州臺登北谷大破吐蕃青海、臘城二節度，斬首二千級，生擒籠官四十五人，其投崖谷而死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Gao sent his great general Wang Youdao to select and drill elite troops for entry into Tibetan territory; together with the eastern barbarians at the North Valley of Taideng in old Xi Prefecture they inflicted a great defeat on the Qinghai and Lachang commands of Tibet, taking two thousand heads, capturing forty-five tribal officers alive, while those who plunged from cliffs and ravines to their deaths were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Gao sent General Wang Youdao to train picked troops and cross into Tibetan territory. Together with the eastern tribes he routed the Qinghai and Lachang Tibetan commands at the North Valley of Taideng in old Xi Prefecture, taking two thousand heads and forty-five officers alive, while countless others perished falling from cliffs and ravines.

sentences.zh: 蕃將乞臧遮遮者，蕃之驍將也，久為邊患。

translations.literal: The Tibetan general Qizang Zhezhe was Tibet's fiercest warrior and had long been a scourge on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan general Qizang Zhezhe was Tibet's most formidable fighter and had long terrorized the border.

sentences.zh: 自擒遮遮，城柵無不降，數年之內，終復巂州，以功加吏部尚書。

translations.literal: From the time Zhezhe was captured, no fort or stockade failed to submit; within several years Xi Prefecture was finally recovered, and for his merit Gao was promoted to minister of civil office appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhezhe was captured, fort after fort surrendered. Within a few years Xi Prefecture was recovered, and Gao was promoted to minister of civil office appointments for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 九年，朝廷築鹽州城，慮為吐蕃掩襲，詔臯出兵牽維之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the court built the city of Yan Prefecture and, fearing a Tibetan surprise attack, ordered Gao to send troops to pin them down.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the court fortified Yan Prefecture. Fearing a Tibetan raid, it ordered Gao to launch operations that would tie down Tibetan forces.

sentences.zh: 乃命大將董勔、張芬出西山及南道，破峨和城、通鶴軍。

translations.literal: He then ordered the great generals Dong Kan and Zhang Fen to advance by the western mountains and the southern route, capturing Ehe City and Tonghe Army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Generals Dong Kan and Zhang Fen along the western mountains and the southern route, capturing Ehe City and the Tonghe garrison.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃南道元帥論莽熱率眾來援，又破之，殺傷數千人，焚定廉城。

translations.literal: The Tibetan southern-route commander Lun Mangre led his forces to the rescue; they were defeated again, with several thousand killed or wounded, and Dinglian City was burned.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan southern commander Lun Mangre marched to relieve them but was defeated again, with thousands killed or wounded, and Dinglian City was burned.

sentences.zh: 凡平堡柵五十余所，以功進位檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In all more than fifty forts and stockades were taken; for his merit he was advanced to acting right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty forts and stockades were taken in all. For this he was promoted to acting right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 臯又招撫西山羌女、訶陵、白狗、逋租、弱水、南王等八國酋長，入貢闕廷。

translations.literal: Gao also won over the chieftains of the eight western mountain states—Qiangnu, Heling, Baigou, Bozu, Ruoshui, Nanwang, and others—to present tribute at the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: Gao also won over the chieftains of eight western mountain peoples—among them Qiangnu, Heling, Baigou, Bozu, Ruoshui, and Nanwang—who came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月，加統押近界諸蠻、西山八國兼雲南安撫等使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year he was additionally appointed commissioner for overseeing the nearby barbarians, the eight western mountain states, and Yunnan pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year he received the additional post of commissioner overseeing nearby tribes, the eight western mountain states, and Yunnan pacification.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，就加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year he was further appointed associate chief minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year he was made associate chief minister on the spot.

sentences.zh: 十三年，收復巂州城。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the city of Xi Prefecture was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the city of Xi Prefecture was recovered.

sentences.zh: 十六年，臯命將出軍，累破吐蕃於黎、巂二州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Gao ordered his generals to take the field and repeatedly defeated the Tibetans in Li and Xi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Gao sent his generals into the field and repeatedly defeated Tibetan forces in Li and Xi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃怒，遂大搜閱，築壘造舟，欲謀入寇，臯悉挫之。

translations.literal: Tibet grew angry and undertook a general mobilization, building ramparts and constructing boats, intending to plan an invasion; Gao thwarted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Tibet mobilized on a large scale, building fortifications and boats for a planned invasion, but Gao foiled every move.

sentences.zh: 於是吐蕃酋帥兼監統曩貢、臘城等九節度嬰、籠官馬定德與其大將八十七人舉部落來降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Tibetan chieftain and overseer of the Nangong, Lachang, and other nine commands, Ying, the tribal officer Ma Dingde, and eighty-seven of his great generals brought their tribes in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Tibetan chieftain who oversaw the Nangong, Lachang, and eight other commands, Ying, the tribal officer Ma Dingde, and eighty-seven senior generals surrendered with their tribes.

sentences.zh: 定德有計略，習知兵法及山川地形，吐蕃每用兵，定德常乘驛計事，蕃中諸將稟其成算。

translations.literal: Dingde was resourceful in stratagem and thoroughly versed in military doctrine and the terrain of mountains and rivers; whenever Tibet took the field, Dingde would often ride the post relays to plan affairs, and the Tibetan generals all followed his completed calculations.
translations.idiomatic: Dingde was a skilled strategist who knew military doctrine and mountain terrain intimately. Whenever Tibet went to war, he often rode the post relays to plan campaigns, and Tibetan generals followed his designs.

sentences.zh: 至是，自以扞邊失律，懼得罪而歸心焉。

translations.literal: At this point, believing himself to have failed in defending the frontier and fearing punishment, he turned his heart toward submission.
translations.idiomatic: Now, believing he had failed on the frontier and fearing punishment, he turned to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十七年，吐蕃昆明城管些蠻千余戶又降。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year more than a thousand households of the Guanxi barbarians under Tibetan Kunming City also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year more than a thousand households of the Guanxi tribes under Tibetan Kunming City also surrendered.

sentences.zh: 贊普以其眾外潰，遂北寇靈、朔，陷麟州。

translations.literal: The tsenpo, because his forces had collapsed abroad, then raided north into Ling and Shuozhou and captured Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With his southwestern forces collapsing, the Tibetan emperor turned north to raid Ling and Shuozhou and captured Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德宗遣使至成都府，令臯出兵深入蕃界。

translations.literal: Dezong sent envoys to Chengdu and ordered Gao to send troops deep into Tibetan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong sent envoys to Chengdu ordering Gao to march deep into Tibetan territory.

sentences.zh: 臯乃令鎮靜軍使陳洎等統兵萬人出三奇路，威戎軍使崔堯臣兵千人出龍溪石門路南，維保二州兵馬使仇冕、保霸二州刺史董振等兵二千趨吐蕃維州城中，北路兵馬使邢玼等四千趨吐蕃棲雞、老翁城，都將高倜、王英俊兵二千趨故松州，隴東兵馬使元膺兵八千人出南道雅、邛、黎、巂路。

translations.literal: Gao then ordered the Zhenjing Army commissioner Chen Ji and others to command ten thousand men out the Sanqi route; the Weirong Army commissioner Cui Yaochan with one thousand men out the Longxi Shimen southern route; the Wei and Bao circuit troop commissioners Qiu Mian, the Bao and Ba prefects Dong Zhen, and others with two thousand men toward the Tibetan city of Wei Prefecture; the northern-route troop commissioner Xing Qi and others with four thousand toward the Tibetan cities of Qiji and Laoweng; the commanders Gao Tong and Wang Yingjun with two thousand toward old Song Prefecture; and the Longdong troop commissioner Yuan Ying with eight thousand men out the southern route through Ya, Qiong, Li, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao deployed his forces on several axes: Chen Ji led ten thousand men along the Sanqi route; Cui Yaochan led one thousand along the Longxi Shimen southern road; Qiu Mian and Dong Zhen led two thousand against the Tibetan city of Wei Prefecture; Xing Qi led four thousand against Qiji and Laoweng; Gao Tong and Wang Yingjun led two thousand toward old Song Prefecture; and Yuan Ying led eight thousand along the southern route through Ya, Qiong, Li, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 又令鎮南軍使韋良金兵一千三百續進，雅州經略使路惟明等兵三千趨吐蕃租、松等城，黎州經略使王有道兵二千人過大渡河，深入蕃界，巂州經略使陳孝陽、兵馬使何大海、韋義等及磨些蠻、東蠻二部落主苴那時等兵四千進攻昆明城、諾濟城。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Zhennan Army commissioner Wei Liangjin with thirteen hundred men to advance in support; the Ya circuit commissioner Lu Weiming and others with three thousand toward the Tibetan cities of Zu and Song; the Li circuit commissioner Wang Youdao with two thousand to cross the Dadu River and penetrate deep into Tibetan territory; and the Xi circuit commissioner Chen Xiaoyang, the troop commissioners He Dahai and Wei Yi, together with the Mosuo and eastern barbarian tribal lords Junashi and others with four thousand to attack Kunming City and Nuoji City.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangjin followed with thirteen hundred men. Lu Weiming led three thousand against Zu and Song; Wang Youdao led two thousand across the Dadu River deep into Tibetan lands; and Chen Xiaoyang, He Dahai, Wei Yi, and the Mosuo and eastern tribal chief Junashi led four thousand against Kunming and Nuoji.

sentences.zh: 自八月出軍齊入，至十月破蕃兵十六萬，拔城七、軍鎮五、戶三千，擒生六千，斬首萬余級，遂進攻維州。

translations.literal: From the eighth month the armies marched in together; by the tenth month they had defeated one hundred sixty thousand Tibetan troops, taken seven cities, five garrisons, and three thousand households, captured six thousand alive, and cut off more than ten thousand heads, then pressed the attack on Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The armies marched out together in the eighth month. By the tenth month they had routed 160,000 Tibetan troops, taken seven cities and five garrisons, captured three thousand households and six thousand prisoners, and severed more than ten thousand heads, then advanced on Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 救軍再至，轉戰千里，蕃軍連敗。

translations.literal: Relief forces came again and again; fighting ranged over a thousand li, and the Tibetan army suffered defeat after defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Relief columns arrived repeatedly, but after battles across a thousand li the Tibetan forces kept losing.

sentences.zh: 於是寇靈、朔之眾引而南下，贊普遣論莽熱以內大相兼東境五道節度兵馬都群牧大使，率雜虜十萬而來解維州之圍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the forces that had raided Ling and Shuozhou turned south; the tsenpo sent Lun Mangre as inner chief minister and concurrently eastern-border five-circuit military governor and grand herds commissioner, leading one hundred thousand mixed barbarians to relieve the siege of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The troops that had raided Ling and Shuozhou now turned south. The Tibetan emperor sent Lun Mangre, serving as inner chief minister and eastern-border commander, with one hundred thousand allied tribesmen to break the siege of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蜀師萬人據險設伏以待之，先出千人挑戰。

translations.literal: Ten thousand Shu troops took strong positions and set an ambush to await them, first sending out one thousand men to offer challenge.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand Shu troops took the high ground and laid an ambush, first sending out a thousand men to provoke a fight.

sentences.zh: 莽熱見我師之少，悉眾追之。

translations.literal: Mangre, seeing how few our troops were, pursued with his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how few Tang troops there were, Mangre pursued with his whole army.

sentences.zh: 發伏掩擊，鼓噪雷駭，蕃兵自潰，生擒論莽熱，虜眾十萬，殲夷者半。

translations.literal: The ambush was sprung; with drums and shouts like thunder the Tibetan troops collapsed of themselves; Lun Mangre was captured alive; of the barbarian host of one hundred thousand, half were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush struck. Drums and shouts rolled like thunder and the Tibetan army broke. Lun Mangre was captured alive. Of the hundred thousand enemy troops, half were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，遣使獻論莽熱於朝；

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year envoys were sent to present Lun Mangre at court;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year Gao sent Lun Mangre to the capital as a captive;

sentences.zh: 德宗數而釋之，賜第於崇仁裏。

translations.literal: Dezong rebuked him and then released him, granting him a residence in Chongren Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong rebuked him, then released him and granted him a house in Chongren Lane.

sentences.zh: 臯以功加檢校司徒，兼中書令，封南康郡王。

translations.literal: For his merit Gao was promoted to acting minister of works, concurrently director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements Gao was made acting minister of works and director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, Gao was further appointed acting grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, Gao was further appointed acting grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 順宗久疾，不能臨朝聽政，宦者李忠言、侍棋待詔王叔文、侍書待詔王伾等三人頗幹國政，高下在心。

translations.literal: Shunzong had long been ill and could not attend court to hear government; the eunuch Li Zhongyan, the chess attendant Wang Shuwen, and the calligraphy attendant Wang Pi—these three men—handled state affairs to a considerable degree, raising or lowering matters as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong had been ill for a long time and could not preside over court. The eunuch Li Zhongyan, the chess attendant Wang Shuwen, and the calligraphy attendant Wang Pi largely ran state affairs as they saw fit.

sentences.zh: 臯乃遣支度副使劉辟使於京師，辟私謁王叔文曰：「太尉使致誠於足下，若能致某都領劍南三川，必有以相酬；

translations.literal: Gao then sent his revenue deputy commissioner Liu Bi as envoy to the capital; Bi privately visited Wang Shuwen and said, "The Grand Preceptor sends his sincerity to you—if you can secure for me command of the three Jiannan circuits, there will certainly be reward;
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent his revenue deputy Liu Bi to the capital. Bi privately visited Wang Shuwen and said, "The Grand Preceptor sends his regards. If you can secure command of the three Jiannan circuits for him, he will reward you handsomely;

sentences.zh: 如不留意，亦有以奉報。」

translations.literal: if you do not heed this, there is also a way to repay you nonetheless."
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse, he has other ways to repay you."

sentences.zh: 叔文大怒，將斬辟以徇；

translations.literal: Shuwen was furious and was about to behead Bi as a warning;
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was furious and was about to execute Bi as a warning;

sentences.zh: 韋執誼固止之，辟乃私去。

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyi firmly stopped him, and Bi slipped away in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi restrained him, and Bi slipped away.

sentences.zh: 臯知王叔文人情不附，又知與韋執誼有隙，自以大臣可議社稷大計，乃上表請皇太子監國，曰：「臣聞上承宗廟，下鎮黎元，永固無疆，莫先儲兩。

translations.literal: Gao knew that Wang Shuwen lacked popular support and also knew of his rift with Wei Zhiyi; considering himself a chief minister who might discuss the great plans of state, he submitted a memorial asking that the crown prince supervise the state, saying, "Your servant has heard that in upholding the ancestral temples above and securing the black-haired people below, for eternal stability without limit nothing comes before establishing the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Gao knew Shuwen lacked support and that he was at odds with Wei Zhiyi. As a senior minister who could speak to the fate of the realm, he memorialized asking that the crown prince supervise the government: "I have heard that to uphold the ancestral temples above and secure the people below, nothing matters more than a secure heir.

sentences.zh: 伏聞聖明以山陵未祔，哀毀逾制，心勞萬幾，伏計旬月之間，未甚痊復。

translations.literal: I have heard that Your Sageliness, because the imperial tomb has not yet received the spirit tablet, grieves beyond measure and toils at the myriad affairs of state; I venture to estimate that within the space of ten days or a month you have not yet fully recovered.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that Your Majesty, with the imperial tomb not yet enshrined, mourns beyond measure while laboring over every affair of state. I fear that within the coming weeks you have not yet fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 皇太子睿質已長，淑問日彰，四海之心，實所倚賴。

translations.literal: The crown prince's wise nature has already matured, his fine reputation grows daily, and the hearts of the four seas truly rely upon him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's wisdom has matured, his reputation grows daily, and the empire truly relies upon him.

sentences.zh: 伏望權令皇太子監撫庶政，以俟聖躬痊平，一日萬幾，免令壅滯。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will temporarily authorize the crown prince to oversee the myriad affairs of government, until Your Sagely Person recovers, so that the ten thousand matters of a single day will not be obstructed and delayed."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that the crown prince be empowered to oversee government until Your Majesty recovers, so that the myriad affairs of state will not pile up unattended."

sentences.zh: 又上皇太子箋曰：

translations.literal: He also submitted a letter to the crown prince, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a letter to the crown prince:

sentences.zh: 殿下體重離之德，當儲貳之重，所以克昌九廟，式固萬方，天下安危，系於殿下。

translations.literal: Your Highness embodies the virtue of doubled Li and bears the weight of the heir apparent; thereby the nine temples may flourish and the ten thousand regions be secured—the safety and peril of the realm hang upon Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness embodies the virtue of the second hexagram and bears the weight of the heir apparent. Through you the ancestral temples may flourish and the realm be secured. The safety of the empire rests upon you.

sentences.zh: 臯位居將相，誌切匡扶，先朝獎知，早承恩顧。

translations.literal: Gao stands in the ranks of generals and ministers, his will set on supporting and upholding you; the former court praised and knew him, and he early received gracious favor.
translations.idiomatic: I stand among your generals and ministers, resolved to support you. The late emperor favored me, and I have long enjoyed imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 人臣之分，知無不為，願上答眷私，罄輸肝鬲。

translations.literal: The duty of a subject is to do whatever he knows should be done; I wish to repay your private favor above and pour out my liver and spleen entirely.
translations.idiomatic: A subject's duty is to act on whatever he knows must be done. I wish to repay your kindness and lay bare my whole heart.

sentences.zh: 伏以聖上嗣膺鴻業，睿哲英明，攀感先朝，誌存孝理。

translations.literal: I submit that Your Sagely Majesty has succeeded to the great enterprise, wise and perspicacious, clinging in grief to the former court and resolved upon the principles of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has succeeded to the great enterprise, wise and perspicacious, clinging in grief to the late emperor and devoted to filial duty.

sentences.zh: 諒闇之際，方委大臣，但付托偶失於善人，而參決多虧於公政。

translations.literal: In this period of deep mourning he has just entrusted affairs to chief ministers, yet the commission has by chance fallen upon unworthy men, and their participation in decisions has largely harmed public government.
translations.idiomatic: In this period of mourning he has entrusted affairs to his ministers, but power has fallen by mischance into unworthy hands, and their decisions have harmed the public good.

sentences.zh: 今群小得誌，隳紊紀綱，官以勢遷，政由情改，朋黨交構，熒惑宸聰。

translations.literal: Now petty men have gained their wish, destroying and disordering the statutes and regulations; offices shift according to power, government changes according to private feeling; factions weave plots and dazzle the imperial ear.
translations.idiomatic: Now petty men have had their way, tearing down law and order. Offices change hands by influence, policy shifts by whim, factions weave plots, and the Son of Heaven's judgment is clouded.

sentences.zh: 樹置腹心，遍於貴位；

translations.literal: they plant their intimates throughout the lofty posts;
translations.idiomatic: they plant their intimates throughout the highest offices;

sentences.zh: 潛結左右，難在蕭墻。

translations.literal: they secretly bind those at the emperor's side—the peril lies within the palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: they secretly bind those around the throne—the danger is within the palace itself.

sentences.zh: 國賦散於權門，王稅不入天府，褻慢無忌，高下在心。

translations.literal: The state's levies are scattered among powerful houses; the royal taxes do not enter the celestial treasury; they are irreverent without restraint, raising or lowering matters as they please.
translations.idiomatic: State revenue is scattered among powerful houses; royal taxes never reach the treasury. They are brazen beyond measure and do as they please.

sentences.zh: 貨賄流聞，遷轉失敘，先聖屏黜贓犯之類，鹹擢居省寺之間。

translations.literal: Bribery circulates openly; promotions and transfers lose all order; men whom the former sage had banished as corrupt criminals are all elevated among the ministries and directorates.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes circulate openly; promotions lose all order. Men the late emperor had banished as corrupt criminals now sit in the ministries and directorates.

sentences.zh: 至令忠臣隕涕，正人結舌，遐邇痛心，人知不可。

translations.literal: This has brought loyal ministers to shed tears, upright men to seal their lips, and grief to near and far alike—all know this cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers weep, upright men fall silent, and grief spreads near and far. Everyone knows this cannot continue.

sentences.zh: 伏恐奸雄乘便，因此謀動干戈，危殿下之家邦，傾太宗之王業。

translations.literal: I fear that treacherous heroes may seize the opportunity and on this account plot to stir weapons of war, endangering Your Highness's house and state and overturning Taizong's royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that villains may seize the moment, take up arms, endanger Your Highness's realm, and overturn the empire Taizong built.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太宗櫛沐風雨，經營廟朝，將垂二百年，欲及千萬祀；

translations.literal: I submit that Taizong, bathed in wind and rain, built up the ancestral temples and court, intending his line to endure two hundred years and reach ten thousand generations of sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong endured wind and rain to build the temples and the court, intending his line to endure two hundred years and reach ten thousand generations;

sentences.zh: 而一朝使叔文奸佞之徒，侮弄朝政，恣其胸臆，坐致傾危。

translations.literal: yet in a single morning men like the treacherous Shuwen have been allowed to mock and toy with court government, indulging their private hearts until ruin sits idle before us.
translations.idiomatic: yet in a single morning men like the treacherous Shuwen have been allowed to mock the court, indulge their whims, and bring ruin upon us all.

sentences.zh: 臣每思之，痛心疾首！

translations.literal: Whenever your servant thinks of this, his heart aches and his head burns with pain!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of this, my heart aches and my head burns with grief!

sentences.zh: 伏望殿下斥逐群小，委任賢良，悽悽血誠，輸寫於此！

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Highness will drive out the petty men and entrust affairs to the worthy and good; in bitter, bloody sincerity I pour it all forth here!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to drive out these petty men and entrust power to the worthy. In bitter sincerity I pour out my whole heart here!

sentences.zh: 太子優令答之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince You ordered a reply to be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Li You ordered a reply.

sentences.zh: 而裴均、嚴綬箋表繼至，由是政歸太子，盡逐伾文之黨。

translations.literal: Then memorial letters from Pei Jun and Yan Shou arrived in succession; from this the government returned to the Crown Prince, and all of Shuwen's faction were driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial letters from Pei Jun and Yan Shou then arrived in succession. Power returned to the Crown Prince, and Shuwen's entire faction was driven out.

sentences.zh: 是歲，暴疾卒，時年六十一，贈太師，廢朝五日。

translations.literal: That year he died suddenly of illness, aged sixty-one; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor, and court was suspended for five days.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died suddenly of illness at the age of sixty-one. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor, and court was suspended for five days.

sentences.zh: 臯在蜀二十一年，重賦斂以事月進，卒致蜀土虛竭，時論非之。

translations.literal: Gao was in Shu for twenty-one years, levying heavy taxes to supply the monthly tribute to the capital, ultimately leaving the land of Shu drained empty; contemporary opinion criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Gao governed Shu for twenty-one years, levying heavy taxes to supply the monthly tribute to the capital until the province was drained. Contemporary opinion condemned him for it.

sentences.zh: 其從事累官稍崇者，則奏為屬郡刺史，或又署在府幕，多不令還朝，蓋不欲泄所為於闕下故也。

translations.literal: Those among his staff who rose in rank he would memorialize for appointment as prefect of a subordinate commandery, or else place them in his office staff, mostly not allowing them to return to court—presumably because he did not wish his actions to leak out at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Staff members who rose in rank he would have appointed prefect of a subordinate commandery, or else keep in his office, mostly forbidding them to return to court—presumably so that his doings would not reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 故劉辟因臯故態，圖不軌以求三川，歷階之作，蓋有由然。

translations.literal: Hence Liu Pi, taking advantage of Gao's old pattern, plotted rebellion to seize the Three River regions; his step-by-step rise surely had its causes.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Liu Pi, following Gao's old example, plotted rebellion to seize the Three River regions. His step-by-step rise surely had its causes.

sentences.zh: 臯兄 聿臯兄聿，時為國子司業，劉辟與盧文若據西川叛，臯侄行式，先娶文若妹，而聿不奏。

translations.literal: Gao's elder brother Yu—Gao's elder brother Yu—at the time served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education; when Liu Pi and Lu Wenruo held West River and rebelled, Gao's nephew Xingshi had earlier married Wenruo's sister, yet Yu did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's elder brother Yu, who at the time served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education: when Liu Pi and Lu Wenruo held West River and rebelled, Gao's nephew Xingshi had already married Wenruo's sister, yet Yu did not report it.

sentences.zh: 既收行式，以其妻沒官，詔御史臺按聿，聿下獄。

translations.literal: Once Xingshi was arrested, his wife was confiscated to become state property; an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate Yu, and Yu was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xingshi was arrested, his wife was confiscated to the state. An edict ordered the Censorate to investigate Yu, and Yu was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 有司以行式妻在遠，不與兄同情，不當連坐，詔歸行式妻而釋聿。

translations.literal: The authorities ruled that because Xingshi's wife was far away and did not share her brother-in-law's sympathy, she should not suffer collective punishment; an edict returned Xingshi's wife and released Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities ruled that because Xingshi's wife was far away and did not share her brother-in-law's sentiments, she should not be punished by association. An edict returned Xingshi's wife and released Yu.

sentences.zh: 劉辟者，貞元中進士擢第，宏詞登科，韋臯辟為從事，累遷至御史中丞、支度副使。

translations.literal: Liu Pi, in the Zhenyuan era passed the jinshi examination and succeeded in the Hongci examination; Wei Gao recruited him as a staff member, and he was promoted in succession to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Deputy Commissioner for Revenue and Expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi passed the jinshi examination in the Zhenyuan era and succeeded in the Hongci examination. Wei Gao recruited him as a staff member, and he rose in succession to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Deputy Commissioner for Revenue and Expenditure.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年八月，韋臯卒，辟自為西川節度留後，率成都將校上表請降節鉞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongzhen, Wei Gao died; Pi made himself acting military governor of West River, leading Chengdu officers in a memorial requesting investiture with the seal and battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongzhen 1, when Wei Gao died, Liu Pi made himself acting military governor of West River and led Chengdu officers in a memorial requesting the seal and battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不許，除給事中，便令赴闕。

translations.literal: The court did not approve, but appointed him Palace Reminder and ordered him to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not approve. Instead it appointed him Palace Reminder and ordered him to come to the capital.

sentences.zh: 辟不奉詔。

translations.literal: Pi did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Pi did not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 時憲宗初即位，以無事息人為務，遂授辟檢校工部尚書，充劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Xianzong had just ascended the throne and made non-aggression and calming the people his priority; he therefore granted Pi the post of Inspector-General Minister of Works and appointed him military governor of Jiannan West River.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Emperor Xianzong had just ascended the throne and made peace and the welfare of the people his priority. He therefore granted Pi the post of Inspector-General Minister of Works and appointed him military governor of Jiannan West River.

sentences.zh: 辟益兇悖，出不臣之言，而求都統三川，與同幕盧文若相善，欲以文若為東川節度使，遂舉兵圍梓州。

translations.literal: Pi grew ever more violent and insolent, uttering disloyal words and demanding overall command of the Three River regions; he was on good terms with his fellow staff member Lu Wenruo and wished to make Wenruo military governor of East River, whereupon he raised troops and besieged Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pi grew ever more violent and insolent, uttering disloyal words and demanding overall command of the Three River regions. On good terms with his fellow staff member Lu Wenruo, he wished to make Wenruo military governor of East River and raised troops to besiege Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 憲宗難於用兵，宰相杜黃裳奏：「劉辟一狂蹶書生耳，王師鼓行而俘之，兵不血刃。

translations.literal: Xianzong was reluctant to use troops; the chief minister Du Huangchang memorialized: "Liu Pi is merely a wild, frantic bookworm. Imperial troops marching in order can capture him without blades being bloodied.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was reluctant to use troops. The chief minister Du Huangchang memorialized: "Liu Pi is merely a wild, frantic bookworm. Imperial troops marching in order can capture him without blades being bloodied.

sentences.zh: 臣知神策軍使高崇文，驍果可任，舉必成功。」

translations.literal: Your servant knows the Shence Army commissioner Gao Chongwen—bold and capable, fit for the task; recommend him and success is certain."
translations.idiomatic: I know the Shence Army commissioner Gao Chongwen—bold and capable, fit for the task. Recommend him and success is certain."

sentences.zh: 帝數日方從之。

translations.literal: Several days passed before the Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Several days passed before the Emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 於是令高崇文、李元奕將神策京西行營兵相續進發，令與嚴礪、李康掎角相應以討之，仍許其自新。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Gao Chongwen and Li Yuanyi to lead the Shence Capital West expeditionary army to advance in succession, and ordered them to coordinate pincer movements with Yan Li and Li Kang to subdue Pi, still offering him the chance to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered Gao Chongwen and Li Yuanyi to lead the Shence Capital West expeditionary army to advance in succession, coordinating pincer movements with Yan Li and Li Kang to subdue Pi while still offering him the chance to reform.

sentences.zh: 元和元年正月，崇文出師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe, in the first month Chongwen marched out.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe, in the first month Chongwen marched out.

sentences.zh: 三月，收復東川。

translations.literal: In the third month East River was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month East River was recovered.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict was then issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued:

sentences.zh: 朕聞皇祖玄元之誡曰：「兵者，兇器也，不得已而用之。」

translations.literal: I have heard our imperial ancestor the Mysterious Ancestor's admonition: "Arms are instruments of violence; one uses them only when there is no alternative."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard our imperial ancestor the Mysterious Ancestor's admonition: "Arms are instruments of violence; one uses them only when there is no alternative."

sentences.zh: 恭惟聖謨，常所祗服。

translations.literal: I reverently hold this sacred design in constant esteem.
translations.idiomatic: I reverently hold this sacred teaching in constant esteem.

sentences.zh: 故惟文誥有所不至，誠信有所未孚，始務安人，必能忍恥，朕之此誌，亦可明征。

translations.literal: Therefore even when written decrees did not reach him and trust was not fully established, I first sought to pacify the people and was willing to bear humiliation—this purpose of mine can be clearly seen.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore even when written decrees did not reach him and trust was not fully established, I first sought to pacify the people and was willing to bear humiliation. This purpose of mine can be clearly seen.

sentences.zh: 近者德宗皇帝舉柔服之規，授宰衡之傑，弘我廟勝，遂康巴、庸，故得南詔入貢，西戎寢患。

translations.literal: Recently Emperor Dezong adopted a policy of gentle accommodation and entrusted a foremost statesman, extending our plan of victory at the ancestral temple; Ba and Yong were thus pacified, Nanzhao came to pay tribute, and the troubles of the western barbarians subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Emperor Dezong adopted a policy of gentle accommodation and entrusted a foremost statesman, extending our plan of victory at the ancestral temple. Ba and Yong were pacified, Nanzhao came to pay tribute, and the troubles of the western barbarians subsided.

sentences.zh: 成績始究，元臣喪亡，劉辟乘此變故，坐邀符節。

translations.literal: His achievements were just reaching completion when the great minister died; Liu Pi seized on this turn of events and boldly demanded the command seal.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were just reaching completion when the great minister died. Liu Pi seized on this turn of events and boldly demanded the command seal.

sentences.zh: 朕以成狂命者雖乖於理體，從權便者所冀於輯寧，竟乖卿士之謀，遂允幸求之誌。

translations.literal: I considered that fulfilling a mad petition would violate proper principle, yet exercising expedient power I hoped for restoration of peace; in the end I went against my ministers' counsel and granted his presumptuous request.
translations.idiomatic: I considered that fulfilling a mad petition would violate proper principle, yet by exercising expedient power I hoped for restoration of peace. In the end I went against my ministers' counsel and granted his presumptuous request.

sentences.zh: 朕之於辟，恩亦弘矣。

translations.literal: My favor toward Pi was already great.
translations.idiomatic: My favor toward Pi was already great.

sentences.zh: 曾不知恩，負牛羊之力，飽則逾兇；

translations.literal: He never knew gratitude; like an ox or sheep fed until sated, he grew all the more savage;
translations.idiomatic: he never knew gratitude; like an ox or sheep fed until sated, he grew all the more savage;

sentences.zh: 畜梟獍之心，馴之益悖。

translations.literal: he nursed the heart of an owl-devouring beast; the more he was indulged, the more rebellious he became.
translations.idiomatic: he nursed the heart of an owl-devouring beast; the more he was indulged, the more rebellious he became.

sentences.zh: 誑惑士伍，圍逼梓州；

translations.literal: he deceived and stirred the ranks of soldiers and besieged Zizhou;
translations.idiomatic: he deceived and stirred the ranks of soldiers and besieged Zizhou;

sentences.zh: 誘陷戎臣，塞絕劍路。

translations.literal: he enticed and trapped frontier officials and blocked the road to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: he enticed and trapped frontier officials and blocked the road to Jian.

sentences.zh: 師徒所至，燒劫無遺，幹紀之辜，擢發難數。

translations.literal: Wherever his army went nothing was left unburned or unplundered; his crimes against law and order are too many to count even strand by strand of hair.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his army went nothing was left unburned or unplundered. His crimes against law and order are too many to count even strand by strand of hair.

sentences.zh: 朕為人司牧，字彼黎元，如辟之罪，非朕敢舍，可削奪在身官爵。

translations.literal: I am shepherd to the people and must protect the black-haired masses; for crimes such as Pi's, I dare not pardon him—let all offices and ranks he currently holds be stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: I am shepherd to the people and must protect the black-haired masses. For crimes such as Pi's, I dare not pardon him. Let all offices and ranks he currently holds be stripped away.

sentences.zh: 六月，崇文破鹿頭關，進收漢州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Chongwen broke through Loutou Pass and advanced to recover Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Chongwen broke through Loutou Pass and advanced to recover Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，崇文收成都府。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chongwen took Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chongwen took Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 劉辟以數十騎遁走，投水不死；

translations.literal: Liu Pi fled with several dozen horsemen; he threw himself into the water but did not die;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi fled with several dozen horsemen. He threw himself into the water but did not die;

sentences.zh: 騎將酈定進入水，擒辟於成都府西洋灌田。

translations.literal: the cavalry officer Li Dingjin entered the water and captured Pi in the irrigation fields west of Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: the cavalry officer Li Dingjin entered the water and captured Pi in the irrigation fields west of Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 盧文若先自刃其妻子，然後縋石投江，失其屍。

translations.literal: Lu Wenruo first killed his wife and children with his own blade, then lowered himself with a stone into the river; his corpse was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenruo first killed his wife and children with his own blade, then lowered himself with a stone into the river. His corpse was never found.

sentences.zh: 辟檻送京師，在路飲食自若，以為不當死。

translations.literal: Pi was sent to the capital in a caged cart; on the road he ate and drank as usual, believing he did not deserve death.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was sent to the capital in a caged cart. On the road he ate and drank as usual, believing he did not deserve death.

sentences.zh: 及至京西臨臯驛，左右神策兵士迎之，以帛系首及手足，曳而入，乃驚曰：「何至於是？」

translations.literal: When he reached the Lingao post station west of the capital, Left and Right Shence soldiers came to receive him; they bound his head and limbs with silk and dragged him in. He cried out in alarm: "How can it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Lingao post station west of the capital, Left and Right Shence soldiers came to receive him. They bound his head and limbs with silk and dragged him in. He cried out in alarm: "How can it come to this?"

sentences.zh: 或紿之曰：「國法當爾，無憂也。」

translations.literal: Someone deceived him, saying: "That is what the law requires—have no fear."
translations.idiomatic: Someone deceived him, saying: "That is what the law requires—have no fear."

sentences.zh: 是日，詔曰：「劉辟生於士族，敢蓄梟心，驅劫蜀人，拒扞王命。

translations.literal: That day an edict said: "Liu Pi was born into the gentry class, yet dared to harbor an owl's heart; he drove and plundered the people of Shu and resisted the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict said: "Liu Pi was born into the gentry class, yet dared to harbor treacherous intent. He drove and plundered the people of Shu and resisted the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 肆其狂逆，詿誤一州，俾我黎元，肝腦塗地。

translations.literal: He indulged his wild rebellion, misleading an entire province and leaving our black-haired masses with their livers and brains smeared upon the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged his wild rebellion, misleading an entire province and leaving our people with their livers and brains smeared upon the ground.

sentences.zh: 賊將崔綱等同惡相扇，至死不回，咸宜伏辜，以正刑典。

translations.literal: The rebel generals Cui Gang and others fanned one another's evil and would not turn back even unto death; all should suffer punishment to uphold the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel generals Cui Gang and others fanned one another's evil and would not turn back even unto death. All should suffer punishment to uphold the penal code.

sentences.zh: 劉辟男超郎等九人，並處斬。」

translations.literal: Liu Pi's sons Chaolang and the other nine were all executed."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi's sons Chaolang and the other nine were all executed."

sentences.zh: 辟入京城，上御興安樓受俘馘，令中使於樓下詰辟反狀。

translations.literal: Pi entered the capital; the Emperor ascended Xing'an Tower to receive the captive and severed heads, and ordered a palace envoy below the tower to interrogate Pi on the facts of his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Pi entered the capital. The Emperor ascended Xing'an Tower to receive the captive and severed heads, and ordered a palace envoy below the tower to interrogate Pi on the facts of his rebellion.

sentences.zh: 辟曰：「臣不敢反，五院子弟為惡，臣不能制。」

translations.literal: Pi said: "Your servant did not dare rebel; the sons of the Five-Yard garrison did evil, and your servant could not control them."
translations.idiomatic: Pi said: "I did not dare rebel. The sons of the Five-Yard garrison did evil, and I could not control them."

sentences.zh: 又遣詰之曰：「朕遣中使送旌節官告，何故不受？」

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent someone to interrogate him: "I sent a palace envoy to deliver the banner, seal, and commission—why did you not accept them?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again sent someone to interrogate him: "I sent a palace envoy to deliver the banner, seal, and commission—why did you not accept them?"

sentences.zh: 辟乃伏罪。

translations.literal: Pi then confessed his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Pi then confessed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 令獻太廟、郊社，徇於市，即日戮於子城西南隅。

translations.literal: He was ordered presented at the Grand Temple and the altars of soil and grain, paraded through the market, and executed that same day at the southwest corner of the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: He was presented at the Grand Temple and the altars of soil and grain, paraded through the market, and executed that same day at the southwest corner of the inner city.

sentences.zh: 初，辟嘗病，見諸問疾者來，皆以手據地，倒行入辟口，辟因礫裂食之；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Pi once fell ill, he saw all who came to inquire after his health place their hands on the ground and crawl backward into Pi's mouth, whereupon Pi would break them into gravel and eat them;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Pi once fell ill, he saw all who came to inquire after his health place their hands on the ground and crawl backward into his mouth, whereupon he would break them into gravel and eat them;

sentences.zh: 惟盧文若至，則如平常。

translations.literal: only when Lu Wenruo came did things appear as usual.
translations.idiomatic: only when Lu Wenruo came did things appear as usual.

sentences.zh: 故尤與文若厚，竟以同惡俱赤族，不其怪歟！

translations.literal: Hence he was especially close to Wenruo, yet in the end both were punished as fellow evildoers and their entire clans exterminated—is this not strange!
translations.idiomatic: Hence he was especially close to Wenruo, yet in the end both were punished as fellow evildoers and their entire clans exterminated—is this not strange!

sentences.zh: 張建封，字本立，兗州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianfeng—Zhang Jianfeng, courtesy name Benli, was a native of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng, whose courtesy name was Benli, came from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖仁範，洪州南昌縣令，貞元初贈鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Renfan was magistrate of Nanchang County in Hongzhou; at the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Renfan was magistrate of Nanchang County in Hongzhou and was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Zhengzhou at the beginning of the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 父玠，少豪俠，輕財重士。

translations.literal: His father Jie in youth was bold and chivalrous, lightly spending wealth and honoring men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jie was bold and chivalrous in youth, freely spending his wealth and honoring men of talent.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，令偽將李庭偉率蕃兵脅下城邑，至魯郡；

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he ordered the false general Li Tingwei to lead barbarian troops in coercing the surrender of cities and towns as far as Lu Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he ordered the false general Li Tingwei to lead barbarian troops in coercing the surrender of cities and towns as far as Lu Commandery;

sentences.zh: 太守韓擇木具禮郊迎，置於郵館。

translations.literal: the prefect Han Zemu received him with full ceremony in the suburban greeting and lodged him in the post station.
translations.idiomatic: the prefect Han Zemu received him with full ceremony in the suburban greeting and lodged him in the post station.

sentences.zh: 玠率鄉豪張貴、孫邑、段絳等集兵將殺之。

translations.literal: Jie led local magnates Zhang Gui, Sun Yi, Duan Jiang, and others to gather troops intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie led local magnates Zhang Gui, Sun Yi, Duan Jiang, and others to gather troops intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 擇木怯懦，大懼；

translations.literal: Zemu was cowardly and greatly afraid;
translations.idiomatic: Zemu was cowardly and greatly afraid;

sentences.zh: 唯員外司兵張孚然其計，遂殺庭偉並其黨數十人，擇木方遣使奏聞。

translations.literal: only the supernumerary army officer Zhang Fu approved the plan; they then killed Tingwei and several dozen of his followers, after which Zemu sent an envoy to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: only the supernumerary army officer Zhang Fu approved the plan. They then killed Tingwei and several dozen of his followers, after which Zemu sent an envoy to report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 擇木、張孚俱受官賞，玠因遊蕩江南，不言其功。

translations.literal: Zemu and Zhang Fu both received offices and rewards; Jie wandered through the Jiangnan region and did not speak of his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zemu and Zhang Fu both received offices and rewards. Jie wandered through the Jiangnan region and did not speak of his achievement.

sentences.zh: 以建封貴，贈秘書監。

translations.literal: Because Jianfeng became eminent, Jie was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jianfeng became eminent, Jie was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建封少頗屬文，好談論，慷慨負氣，以功名為己任。

translations.literal: Jianfeng in youth was fairly skilled in letters, loved discussion, was generous and high-spirited, and took achievement and fame as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng in youth was fairly skilled in letters, loved discussion, and was generous and high-spirited, taking achievement and fame as his own charge.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，李光弼鎮河南，時蘇、常等州草賊，寇掠郡邑，代宗遣中使馬日新與光弼將兵馬同征討之。

translations.literal: In the Baoying era Li Guangbi governed Henan; at that time bandits in Su, Chang, and other prefectures raided and plundered commandery cities, and Emperor Daizong sent the palace envoy Ma Rixin with Guangbi to lead troops jointly to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoying era Li Guangbi governed Henan. At that time bandits in Su, Chang, and other prefectures raided and plundered commandery cities, and Emperor Daizong sent the palace envoy Ma Rixin with Guangbi to lead troops jointly to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 建封乃見日新，自請說喻賊徒。

translations.literal: Jianfeng then went to see Rixin and volunteered to persuade the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng then went to see Rixin and volunteered to persuade the bandits.

sentences.zh: 日新從之，遂入虎窟、蒸裏等賊營，以利害禍福喻之。

translations.literal: Rixin agreed; Jianfeng then entered the bandit camps at Huku, Zhengli, and elsewhere, explaining to them the gains and losses, blessings and disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Rixin agreed. Jianfeng then entered the bandit camps at Huku, Zhengli, and elsewhere, explaining to them the gains and losses, blessings and disasters.

sentences.zh: 一夕，賊黨數千人並詣日新請降，遂悉放歸田裏。

translations.literal: In a single night several thousand bandits all came to Rixin to surrender, and they were all released to return to their fields and villages.
translations.idiomatic: In a single night several thousand bandits all came to Rixin to surrender, and they were all released to return to their fields and villages.

sentences.zh: 大曆初，道州刺史裴虬薦建封於觀察使韋之晉，辟為參謀，奏授左清道兵曹，不樂吏役而去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era the Daozhou prefect Pei Qiu recommended Jianfeng to the observation commissioner Wei Zhijin, who recruited him as a staff adviser; he was memorialized for appointment as Left Qingdao Army Officer, but disliking clerical service he departed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dali era the Daozhou prefect Pei Qiu recommended Jianfeng to the observation commissioner Wei Zhijin, who recruited him as a staff adviser. He was memorialized for appointment as Left Qingdao Army Officer, but disliking clerical service he departed.

sentences.zh: 滑亳節度使令狐彰聞其名，辟之；

translations.literal: The Huabo military governor Linghu Zhang heard his name and recruited him;
translations.idiomatic: The Huabo military governor Linghu Zhang heard his name and recruited him;

sentences.zh: 彰既未曾朝覲，建封心不悅之，遂投刺於轉運使劉晏，自述其誌，不願仕於彰也。

translations.literal: Zhang had never attended court, and Jianfeng was displeased at heart; he therefore presented his calling card to the transport commissioner Liu Yan, stating his own purpose and that he did not wish to serve under Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang had never attended court, and Jianfeng was displeased at heart. He therefore presented his calling card to the transport commissioner Liu Yan, stating his purpose and that he did not wish to serve under Zhang.

sentences.zh: 晏奏試大理評事，勾當軍務。

translations.literal: Yan memorialized to appoint him on probation as Grand Court Assessor in charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yan memorialized to appoint him on probation as Grand Court Assessor in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復罷歸。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was again dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 建封素與馬燧友善，大歷十年，燧為河陽三城鎮遏使，辟為判官，奏授監察御史，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: Jianfeng had long been on friendly terms with Ma Sui; in the tenth year of Dali Sui became commissioner for the defense of the Three Cities of Heyang and recruited Jianfeng as administrative aide; he was memorialized for appointment as surveillance censor and granted the crimson fish pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng had long been on friendly terms with Ma Sui. In the tenth year of Dali Sui became commissioner for the defense of the Three Cities of Heyang and recruited Jianfeng as administrative aide. He was memorialized for appointment as surveillance censor and granted the crimson fish pouch.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜反於梁、宋間，與田悅掎角，同為叛逆，燧與李忠臣同討平之，軍務多咨於建封。

translations.literal: Li Lingyao rebelled between Liang and Song and coordinated pincer movements with Tian Yue as fellow rebels; Sui and Li Zhongchen jointly suppressed and pacified them, and military affairs were largely referred to Jianfeng for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingyao rebelled between Liang and Song and coordinated pincer movements with Tian Yue as fellow rebels. Sui and Li Zhongchen jointly suppressed and pacified them, and military affairs were largely referred to Jianfeng for counsel.

sentences.zh: 及燧為河東節度使，復奏建封為判官，特拜侍御史。

translations.literal: When Sui became military governor of Hedong, he again memorialized for Jianfeng as administrative aide and specially appointed him attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui became military governor of Hedong, he again memorialized for Jianfeng as administrative aide and specially appointed him attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 建中初，燧薦之於朝，楊炎將用為度支郎中，盧杞惡之，出為岳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era Sui recommended him to the court; Yang Yan was about to appoint him Revenue Section Director, but Lu Qi disliked him and had him sent out as prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era Sui recommended him to the court. Yang Yan was about to appoint him Revenue Section Director, but Lu Qi disliked him and had him sent out as prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 時淮西節度使李希烈乘破滅梁崇義之勢，漸縱恣跋扈，壽州刺史崔昭數書疏往來。

translations.literal: At this time the Huai West military governor Li Xilie, riding the momentum of his defeat and destruction of Liang Chongyi, gradually grew wanton and overbearing; the Shouzhou prefect Cui Zhao exchanged numerous letters and memorials with him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Huai West military governor Li Xilie, riding the momentum of his defeat and destruction of Liang Chongyi, gradually grew wanton and overbearing. The Shouzhou prefect Cui Zhao exchanged numerous letters and memorials with him.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使陳少遊奏之，上遽召宰相令選壽州刺史。

translations.literal: The Huainan military governor Chen Shaoyou memorialized about this; the Emperor immediately summoned the chief ministers and ordered them to select a Shouzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan military governor Chen Shaoyou memorialized about this. The Emperor immediately summoned the chief ministers and ordered them to select a Shouzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 盧杞本惡建封，是日蒼黃，遂薦建封以代崔昭牧壽陽。

translations.literal: Lu Qi had long disliked Jianfeng; that day in haste he recommended Jianfeng to replace Cui Zhao as governor of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi had long disliked Jianfeng. That day in haste he recommended Jianfeng to replace Cui Zhao as governor of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 李希烈稱兵，寇陷汝州，擒李元平，擊走胡德信、唐漢臣等，又摧破哥舒曜於襄城，連陷鄭、汴等州，李勉棄城而遁。

translations.literal: Li Xilie raised troops, invaded and captured Ruzhou, seized Li Yuanping, routed Hu Dexin, Tang Hanchen, and others, also crushed Geshu Yao at Xiangcheng, and in succession captured Zheng, Bian, and other prefectures; Li Mian abandoned his city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie raised troops, invaded and captured Ruzhou, seized Li Yuanping, routed Hu Dexin, Tang Hanchen, and others, crushed Geshu Yao at Xiangcheng, and in succession captured Zheng, Bian, and other prefectures. Li Mian abandoned his city and fled.

sentences.zh: 涇師內逆，駕幸奉天，賊鋒益盛。

translations.literal: The Jing troops mutinied within; the Emperor fled to Fengtian, and the rebels' momentum grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing troops mutinied within. The Emperor fled to Fengtian, and the rebels' momentum grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 淮南陳少遊潛通希烈，尋稱偽號，改元，遣將楊豐賫偽赦書二道，令送少遊及建封。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou of Huainan secretly communicated with Xilie; soon Xilie declared a false reign title and changed the era name, sending the general Yang Feng with two false amnesty edicts to deliver to Shaoyou and Jianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou of Huainan secretly communicated with Xilie. Soon Xilie declared a false reign title and changed the era name, sending the general Yang Feng with two false amnesty edicts to deliver to Shaoyou and Jianfeng.

sentences.zh: 至壽州，建封縛楊豐徇於軍中。

translations.literal: When he reached Shouzhou, Jianfeng bound Yang Feng and paraded him before the army.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Shouzhou, Jianfeng bound Yang Feng and paraded him before the army.

sentences.zh: 適會中使自行在及使江南回者同至，建封集眾對中使斬豐於通衢，封偽赦書送行在，遠近震駭。

translations.literal: It happened that palace envoys returning from the imperial camp and from missions to Jiangnan arrived at the same time; Jianfeng assembled the troops and, in the presence of the palace envoys, executed Feng in the public thoroughfare, sealed the false amnesty edicts, and sent them to the imperial camp; near and far were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that palace envoys returning from the imperial camp and from missions to Jiangnan arrived at the same time. Jianfeng assembled the troops and, in the presence of the palace envoys, executed Feng in the public thoroughfare, sealed the false amnesty edicts, and sent them to the imperial camp. Near and far were shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊聞之，既怒且懼。

translations.literal: When Chen Shaoyou heard of this, he was both angry and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shaoyou heard of this, he was both angry and afraid.

sentences.zh: 建封乃具奏少遊與希烈往來事狀。

translations.literal: Jianfeng then submitted a full memorial on the circumstances of Shaoyou's dealings with Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng then submitted a full memorial on the circumstances of Shaoyou's dealings with Xilie.

sentences.zh: 希烈又偽署其黨杜少誠為淮南節度使，令先平壽州，趣江都。

translations.literal: Xilie also falsely appointed his follower Du Shaoqian as Huainan military governor, ordering him first to pacify Shouzhou and then hurry to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie also falsely appointed his follower Du Shaoqian as Huainan military governor, ordering him first to pacify Shouzhou and then hurry to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 建封令其將賀蘭元均、邵怡等守霍丘秋柵。

translations.literal: Jianfeng ordered his generals Helan Yuanjun, Shao Yi, and others to hold the Qiuchai stockade at Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng ordered his generals Helan Yuanjun, Shao Yi, and others to hold the Qiuchai stockade at Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 少誠竟不能侵軼，乃南掠蘄、黃等州，又為伊慎所挫衄。

translations.literal: Shaoqian in the end could not break through; he then raided south through Qi, Huang, and other prefectures, and was again repulsed by Yi Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqian in the end could not break through. He then raided south through Qi, Huang, and other prefectures and was again repulsed by Yi Shen.

sentences.zh: 尋加建封兼御史中丞、本州團練使。

translations.literal: Soon Jianfeng was additionally appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and regimental commissioner of his own prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jianfeng was additionally appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and regimental commissioner of his own prefecture.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，陳少遊憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, Chen Shaoyou died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, Chen Shaoyou died of grief and indignation.

sentences.zh: 興元元年十二月，乃加兼御史大夫，充濠壽廬三州都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Xingyuan he was additionally appointed Censor-in-Chief and made overall regimental and observation commissioner of Hao, Shou, and Lu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Xingyuan he was additionally appointed Censor-in-Chief and made overall regimental and observation commissioner of Hao, Shou, and Lu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 於是大修緝城池，悉心綏撫，遠近悅附，自是威望益重。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly repaired and fortified the city walls, devoted himself to pacification and care, and people near and far gladly attached themselves to him; from this his prestige grew ever weightier.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he greatly repaired and fortified the city walls, devoted himself to pacification and care, and people near and far gladly attached themselves to him. From this his prestige grew ever weightier.

sentences.zh: 李希烈選兇黨精悍者率勁卒以攻建封，曠日持久，無所克獲而去。

translations.literal: Li Xilie selected fierce and able men from his evil faction to lead crack troops against Jianfeng; the siege dragged on day after day without success, and they departed having gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie selected fierce and able men from his faction to lead crack troops against Jianfeng. The siege dragged on day after day without success, and they departed having gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 及希烈平，進階封，賜一子正員官。

translations.literal: When Xilie was pacified, Jianfeng was promoted in rank and enfeoffment, and one of his sons was granted a regular official post.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie was pacified, Jianfeng was promoted in rank and enfeoffment, and one of his sons was granted a regular official post.

sentences.zh: 初，建中年，李涓以徐州歸附。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Jianzhong era, Li Juan submitted Xuzhou in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Jianzhong era, Li Juan submitted Xuzhou in allegiance.

sentences.zh: 涓尋卒，其後高承宗父子、獨孤華相繼為刺史。

translations.literal: Juan soon died; afterward Gao Chengzong and his son, and then Dugu Hua, succeeded one another as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Juan soon died. Afterward Gao Chengzong and his son, and then Dugu Hua, succeeded one another as prefect.

sentences.zh: 為賊侵削，貧困不能自存；

translations.literal: It had been ravaged and stripped by bandits, impoverished and unable to sustain itself;
translations.idiomatic: it had been ravaged and stripped by bandits, impoverished and unable to sustain itself;

sentences.zh: 又咽喉要地，據江淮運路，朝廷思擇重臣以鎮者久之。

translations.literal: moreover it was a vital strategic chokepoint, controlling the Jiang-Huai transport routes; for a long time the court deliberated over choosing a senior minister to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: moreover it was a vital strategic chokepoint, controlling the Jiang-Huai transport routes, and for a long time the court deliberated over choosing a senior minister to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，以建封為徐州刺史，兼御史大夫、徐泗濠節度、支度營田觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, Jianfeng was appointed Prefect of Xuzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Military Commissioner of Xu, Si, and Hao, and Commissioner for fiscal support, military colonies, and observation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, Jianfeng was appointed Prefect of Xuzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Military Commissioner of Xu, Si, and Hao, and Commissioner for fiscal support, military colonies, and observation.

sentences.zh: 既創置軍伍，建封觸事躬親；

translations.literal: Having newly established military units, Jianfeng personally attended to every matter;
translations.idiomatic: Having newly established military units, Jianfeng personally attended to every matter;

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，容納人過誤，而按據綱紀，不妄曲法貸人。

translations.literal: By nature magnanimous, he tolerated people's faults, yet upheld the statutes and never casually bent the law to spare anyone.
translations.idiomatic: By nature magnanimous, he tolerated people's faults, yet upheld the statutes and never casually bent the law to spare anyone.

sentences.zh: 每言事，忠義感激，人皆畏悅。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke on affairs of state, his words stirred with loyal devotion, and all both feared and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke on affairs of state, his words stirred with loyal devotion, and all both feared and delighted in him.

sentences.zh: 七年，進位檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was advanced to Honorary Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, he was advanced to Honorary Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was given the additional title Honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, he was given the additional title Honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，入覲京師，德宗禮遇加等，特以雙日開延英召對，又令朝參入大夫班，以示殊寵。
