translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year he entered the capital for an audience; Dezong treated him with exceptional courtesy, specially convening him for audience in the Hall of Extended Excellence on the double day, and also ordered him to attend court in the senior ministers' rank, as a mark of extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year he entered the capital for an audience. Dezong treated him with exceptional courtesy, specially convening him for audience in the Hall of Extended Excellence on the double day, and also ordered him to attend court in the senior ministers' rank as a mark of extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 建封賦《朝天行》一章上獻，賜名馬珍玩頗厚。

translations.literal: Jianfeng composed and presented a chapter entitled "Journey to Court," and was richly rewarded with fine horses and precious curios.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng composed and presented a chapter entitled "Journey to Court," and was richly rewarded with fine horses and precious curios.

sentences.zh: 時宦者主宮中市買，謂之宮市，抑買人物，稍不如本估。

translations.literal: At that time eunuchs managed purchasing for the palace, calling it the Palace Market; they forced down purchases of goods, paying somewhat less than the original appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: At that time eunuchs managed purchasing for the palace under the name Palace Market, forcing down purchases of goods and paying somewhat less than fair value.

sentences.zh: 末年不復行文書，置白望數十百人於兩市及要鬧坊曲，閱人所賣物；

translations.literal: In the late years they no longer issued written documents, but posted several dozen or a hundred "white watchers" in the two markets and busy wards and alleys to inspect what people were selling;
translations.idiomatic: In the late years they no longer issued written documents, but posted several dozen or a hundred "white watchers" in the two markets and busy wards and alleys to inspect what people were selling;

sentences.zh: 但稱宮市，則斂手付與，真偽不復可辨，無敢問所從來及論價之高下者。

translations.literal: they need only say "Palace Market," and people would fold their hands and surrender the goods; authenticity could no longer be distinguished, and none dared ask whence they came or dispute the price.
translations.idiomatic: They need only say "Palace Market," and people would fold their hands and surrender the goods. Authenticity could no longer be distinguished, and none dared ask whence they came or dispute the price.

sentences.zh: 率用直百錢物買人直數千物，仍索進奉門戶及腳價銀。

translations.literal: As a rule they used goods worth a hundred cash to buy goods worth several thousand, and still demanded gate fees for tribute delivery and porterage silver.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule they used goods worth a hundred cash to buy goods worth several thousand, and still demanded gate fees for tribute delivery and porterage silver.

sentences.zh: 人將物詣市，至有空手而歸者，名為宮市，其實奪之。

translations.literal: When people brought goods to market, some returned empty-handed; it was called the Palace Market, but in truth it was robbery.
translations.idiomatic: When people brought goods to market, some returned empty-handed. It was called the Palace Market, but in truth it was robbery.

sentences.zh: 嘗有農夫以驢馱柴，宦者市之，與絹數尺，又就索門戶，仍邀驢送柴至內。

translations.literal: Once a farmer brought firewood on a donkey; a eunuch "bought" it, giving him several feet of silk, then demanded gate fees and still pressed the donkey to deliver the firewood inside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once a farmer brought firewood on a donkey. A eunuch "bought" it, giving him several feet of silk, then demanded gate fees and still pressed the donkey to deliver the firewood inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 農夫啼泣，以所得絹與之，不肯受，曰：「須得爾驢。」

translations.literal: The farmer wept and offered back the silk he had received, but the eunuch would not accept it, saying: "I must have your donkey."
translations.idiomatic: The farmer wept and offered back the silk he had received, but the eunuch would not accept it, saying, "I must have your donkey."

sentences.zh: 農夫曰：「我有父母妻子，待此而後食；

translations.literal: The farmer said: "I have parents, a wife, and children who depend on this to eat;
translations.idiomatic: The farmer said, "I have parents, a wife, and children who depend on this to eat;

sentences.zh: 今與汝柴，而不取直而歸，汝尚不肯，我有死而已。」

translations.literal: now I have given you my firewood and taken no payment in return, and you still refuse; I have nothing left but to die."
translations.idiomatic: now I have given you my firewood and taken no payment in return, and you still refuse. I have nothing left but to die."

sentences.zh: 遂毆宦者。

translations.literal: Then he beat the eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Then he beat the eunuch.

sentences.zh: 街使擒之以聞，乃黜宦者，賜農夫絹十匹。

translations.literal: The street commissioner seized him and reported the matter; the eunuch was dismissed, and the farmer was granted ten bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The street commissioner seized him and reported the matter. The eunuch was dismissed, and the farmer was granted ten bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 然宮市不為之改，諫宮御史表疏論列，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Yet the Palace Market was not reformed on account of this; memorials and petitions from remonstrating officials and censors were all ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Palace Market was not reformed on account of this. Memorials and petitions from remonstrating officials and censors were all ignored.

sentences.zh: 吳湊以戚裏為京兆尹，深言其弊。

translations.literal: Wu Zou, a relative by marriage of the imperial clan serving as Capital Magistrate, spoke forcefully about its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zou, a relative by marriage of the imperial clan serving as Capital Magistrate, spoke forcefully about its abuses.

sentences.zh: 建封入覲，具奏之，德宗頗深嘉納；

translations.literal: When Jianfeng came to court for an audience, he submitted a full report; Dezong greatly approved and accepted it;
translations.idiomatic: When Jianfeng came to court for an audience, he submitted a full report, and Dezong greatly approved and accepted it;

sentences.zh: 而戶部侍郎、判度支蘇弁希宦者之旨，因入奏事，上問之，弁對曰：「京師遊手墮業者數千萬家，無土著生業，仰宮市取給。」

translations.literal: but Vice Minister of Revenue and fiscal commissioner Su Bian, seeking to please the eunuchs, entered to present affairs, and when the emperor questioned him, Bian replied: "In the capital there are tens of millions of idle households with no fixed livelihood, who depend on the Palace Market for their sustenance."
translations.idiomatic: but Vice Minister of Revenue and fiscal commissioner Su Bian, seeking to please the eunuchs, entered to present affairs, and when the emperor questioned him, Bian replied, "In the capital there are tens of millions of idle households with no fixed livelihood who depend on the Palace Market for their sustenance."

sentences.zh: 上信之，凡言宮市者皆不聽用。

translations.literal: The emperor believed him, and all who spoke about the Palace Market went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him, and all who spoke about the Palace Market went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 詔書矜免百姓諸色逋賦，上問建封，對曰：「凡逋賦殘欠，皆是累積年月，無可征收，雖蒙陛下憂恤，百姓亦無所裨益。」

translations.literal: An edict compassionately remitted the people's various overdue levies; the emperor asked Jianfeng, who replied: "All overdue and outstanding levies are accumulations of many years, with nothing left to collect; though Your Majesty shows compassionate concern, the common people will gain no real benefit."
translations.idiomatic: An edict compassionately remitted the people's various overdue levies. The emperor asked Jianfeng, who replied, "All overdue and outstanding levies are accumulations of many years, with nothing left to collect. Though Your Majesty shows compassionate concern, the common people will gain no real benefit."

sentences.zh: 時河東節度使李說、華州刺史盧微，皆中風疾，口不能言，足不能行，但信任左右胥吏決遣之。

translations.literal: At that time Hedong Military Commissioner Li Shuo and Hua Prefect Lu Wei both suffered strokes; they could not speak with their mouths or walk with their feet, but entrusted all decisions to their clerks and scribes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hedong Military Commissioner Li Shuo and Hua Prefect Lu Wei both suffered strokes. They could not speak with their mouths or walk with their feet, but entrusted all decisions to their clerks and scribes.

sentences.zh: 建封皆悉聞奏，上深嘉納。

translations.literal: Jianfeng reported all of this in full; the emperor greatly approved and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng reported all of this in full, and the emperor greatly approved and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 又金吾大將軍李翰好伺察城中細事，加諸聞奏，冀求恩寵，人畏而惡之。

translations.literal: Also Grand General of the Golden Guard Li Han loved to spy on minor affairs in the city and add them to reports submitted upward, hoping to win imperial favor; people feared and detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Also Grand General of the Golden Guard Li Han loved to spy on minor affairs in the city and add them to reports submitted upward, hoping to win imperial favor. People feared and detested him.

sentences.zh: 建封亦奏之，乃下詔曰：「比來朝官或諸處過從，金吾皆有上聞。

translations.literal: Jianfeng also reported this, whereupon an edict was issued: "Recently, when court officials or others from various places paid visits to one another, the Golden Guard has reported everything upward.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng also reported this, whereupon an edict was issued: "Recently, when court officials or others from various places paid visits to one another, the Golden Guard has reported everything upward.

sentences.zh: 其間如素是親故，或曾同僚友，伏臘歲序，時有還往，亦是常禮，人情所通。

translations.literal: Among such cases, if they were old friends by nature, or former colleagues, seasonal visits at the winter and summer festivals are also ordinary courtesy and what human feeling permits.
translations.idiomatic: Among such cases, if they were old friends by nature or former colleagues, seasonal visits at the winter and summer festivals are also ordinary courtesy and what human feeling permits.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，金吾不須聞。」

translations.literal: From this day forward, the Golden Guard need not report such matters."
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward, the Golden Guard need not report such matters."

sentences.zh: 十四年春上巳，賜宰臣百僚宴於曲江亭，特令建封與宰相同座而食。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year, on the Shangsi festival, the emperor granted a banquet to chief ministers and the hundred officials at Qujiang Pavilion, and specially ordered Jianfeng to sit and eat at the same table as the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourteenth year, on the Shangsi festival, the emperor granted a banquet to chief ministers and the hundred officials at Qujiang Pavilion, and specially ordered Jianfeng to sit and eat at the same table as the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 貞元已後，籓帥入朝及還鎮，如馬燧、渾瑊、劉玄佐、李抱真、曲環之崇秩鴻勛，未有獲禦制詩以送者，建封將還鎮，特賜詩曰：「牧守寄所重，才賢生為時。

translations.literal: After Zhenyuan, when frontier commanders entered court or returned to their posts—men such as Ma Sui, Hun Zhen, Liu Xuanzuo, Li Baozhen, and Qu Huan, honored with lofty rank and great merit—none had ever received an imperially composed poem as a parting gift. As Jianfeng was about to return to his post, he was specially granted a poem that read: "Governors bear the weight entrusted to them; talent and worth are born for their age.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenyuan, when frontier commanders entered court or returned to their posts—men such as Ma Sui, Hun Zhen, Liu Xuanzuo, Li Baozhen, and Qu Huan, honored with lofty rank and great merit—none had ever received an imperially composed poem as a parting gift. As Jianfeng was about to return to his post, he was specially granted a poem that read: "Governors bear the weight entrusted to them; talent and worth are born for their age.

sentences.zh: 宣風自淮甸，授鉞膺籓維。

translations.literal: Spreading virtue from the Huai region, receiving the battle-axe as frontier lord.
translations.idiomatic: Spreading virtue from the Huai region, receiving the battle-axe as frontier lord.

sentences.zh: 入覲展遐戀，臨軒慰來思。

translations.literal: Entering court to show deep longing, at the throne comforting thoughts of return.
translations.idiomatic: Entering court to show deep longing, at the throne comforting thoughts of return.

sentences.zh: 忠誠在方寸，感激陳清詞。

translations.literal: Loyalty fills the heart; moved with gratitude, he states clear words.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty fills the heart; moved with gratitude, he states clear words.

sentences.zh: 報國爾所尚，恤人予是資。

translations.literal: Serving the state is what you honor; caring for the people is what I provide.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the state is what you honor; caring for the people is what I provide.

sentences.zh: 歡宴不盡懷，車馬當還期。

translations.literal: The feast cannot exhaust all feeling; horses must return on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The feast cannot exhaust all feeling; horses must return on schedule.

sentences.zh: 谷雨將應候，行春猶未遲。

translations.literal: Grain Rain will soon answer to the season; the spring journey is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: Grain Rain will soon answer to the season; the spring journey is not yet late.

sentences.zh: 勿以千里遙，而雲無已知。」

translations.literal: Do not, because a thousand li is far, say there is no one who knows you."
translations.idiomatic: Do not, because a thousand li is far, say there is no one who knows you."

sentences.zh: 又令高品中使賫常所執鞭以賜之，曰：「以卿忠貞節義，歲寒不移，此鞭朕久執用，故以賜卿，表卿忠節也。」

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered a high-ranking palace envoy to present the whip he habitually carried and grant it to him, saying: "Because your loyalty, integrity, and steadfastness remain unchanged through cold years, this whip I have long held in use—therefore I give it to you, to show your loyal steadfastness."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered a high-ranking palace envoy to present the whip he habitually carried and grant it to him, saying, "Because your loyalty, integrity, and steadfastness remain unchanged through cold years, this whip I have long held in use—therefore I give it to you, to show your loyal steadfastness."

sentences.zh: 建封又獻詩一篇，以自警勵。

translations.literal: Jianfeng also submitted a poem as self-admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng also submitted a poem as self-admonition.

sentences.zh: 建封在彭城十年，軍州稱理。

translations.literal: Jianfeng was at Pengcheng for ten years; the army and prefecture were said to be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng was at Pengcheng for ten years, and the army and prefecture were said to be well governed.

sentences.zh: 復又禮賢下士，無賢不肖，遊其門者，皆禮遇之，天下名士向風延頸，其往如歸。

translations.literal: Again he honored the worthy and humbled himself before scholars; whether worthy or unworthy, all who came to his gate received courteous treatment; famous men throughout the realm turned their heads toward him and came as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Again he honored the worthy and humbled himself before scholars. Whether worthy or unworthy, all who came to his gate received courteous treatment. Famous men throughout the realm turned their heads toward him and came as if returning home.

sentences.zh: 貞元時，文人如許孟容、韓愈諸公，皆為之從事。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, literary men such as Xu Mengrong, Han Yu, and others all served under him as aides.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era, literary men such as Xu Mengrong, Han Yu, and others all served under him as aides.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遇疾，連上表請速除代，方用韋夏卿為徐泗行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he fell ill and repeatedly submitted memorials requesting swift replacement; Wei Xiaqing was appointed acting army marshal of Xu and Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he fell ill and repeatedly submitted memorials requesting swift replacement. Wei Xiaqing was appointed acting army marshal of Xu and Si.

sentences.zh: 未至而建封卒，時年六十六，冊贈司徒。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Jianfeng died, at the age of sixty-six; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Jianfeng died at the age of sixty-six. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 子愔。

translations.literal: His son Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin.

sentences.zh: 建封子 愔愔以廕授虢州參軍。

translations.literal: Jianfeng's son Yin received by privilege appointment as aide in Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng's son Yin received by privilege appointment as aide in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，建封卒，判官鄭通誠權知留後事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jianfeng died, Judge-Advisor Zheng Tongcheng provisionally managed affairs as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jianfeng died, Judge-Advisor Zheng Tongcheng provisionally managed affairs as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 通誠懼軍士謀亂，適遇浙西兵遷鎮，通誠欲引入州城為援。

translations.literal: Tongcheng feared the soldiers would plot rebellion; it happened that Zhexi troops were redeploying, and Tongcheng wished to bring them into the prefectural city as support.
translations.idiomatic: Tongcheng feared the soldiers would plot rebellion. It happened that Zhexi troops were redeploying, and Tongcheng wished to bring them into the prefectural city as support.

sentences.zh: 事泄，三軍怒，五六千人斫甲仗庫取戈甲，執帶環繞衙城，請愔為留後。

translations.literal: The plot leaked out; the three armies were enraged. Five or six thousand men broke into the armory for weapons and armor, drew their swords, and surrounded the yamen, requesting Yin as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked out, and the three armies were enraged. Five or six thousand men broke into the armory for weapons and armor, drew their swords, and surrounded the yamen, requesting Yin as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乃殺通誠、楊德宗、大將段伯熊、吉遂、曲澄、張秀等。

translations.literal: They then killed Tongcheng, Yang Dezong, and the great generals Duan Boxiong, Ji Sui, Qu Cheng, Zhang Xiu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: They then killed Tongcheng, Yang Dezong, and the great generals Duan Boxiong, Ji Sui, Qu Cheng, Zhang Xiu, and others.

sentences.zh: 軍眾請於朝廷，乞授愔旄節。

translations.literal: The army petitioned the court, begging that Yin be granted the staff of command.
translations.idiomatic: The army petitioned the court, begging that Yin be granted the staff of command.

sentences.zh: 初不之許，乃割濠、泗二州隸淮南，加杜佑同平章事以討徐州。

translations.literal: At first this was not granted; then Hao and Si prefectures were transferred to Huainan, and Du You was made Equal Commissioner to attack Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At first this was not granted. Then Hao and Si prefectures were transferred to Huainan, and Du You was made Equal Commissioner to attack Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而泗州刺史張伾以兵攻埇橋，與徐軍接戰，伾大敗而還。

translations.literal: Then Si Prefect Zhang Fen attacked Yongqiao and clashed with the Xu army; Fen suffered a great defeat and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Then Si Prefect Zhang Fen attacked Yongqiao and clashed with the Xu army. Fen suffered a great defeat and retreated.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不獲已，乃授愔起復右驍衛將軍同正，兼徐州刺史、御史中丞，充本州團練使，知徐州留後。

translations.literal: The court, having no alternative, granted Yin resumed appointment as Right Brave Guards General of equal rank, concurrently Prefect of Xuzhou and Vice Censor-in-Chief, regimental commissioner of the prefecture, and provisional commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court, having no alternative, granted Yin resumed appointment as Right Brave Guards General of equal rank, concurrently Prefect of Xuzhou and Vice Censor-in-Chief, regimental commissioner of the prefecture, and provisional commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 仍以泗州刺史張伾為泗州留後，濠州刺史杜兼為濠州留後。

translations.literal: Zhang Fen was also made provisional commissioner of Si, and Du Jian provisional commissioner of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fen was also made provisional commissioner of Si, and Du Jian provisional commissioner of Hao.

sentences.zh: 正授武寧軍節度、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army and Honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army and Honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，被疾，上表請代，征為兵部尚書，以東都留守王紹為武寧軍節度代愔，復隸濠、泗二州於徐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he fell ill and submitted a memorial requesting replacement; he was recalled as Minister of War, and Wang Shao, Eastern Capital Keeper, was made Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army to replace Yin; Hao and Si were again placed under Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe he fell ill and submitted a memorial requesting replacement. He was recalled as Minister of War, and Wang Shao, Eastern Capital Keeper, was made Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army to replace Yin. Hao and Si were again placed under Xu.

sentences.zh: 徐軍喜復得二州，不敢為亂，而愔遂赴京師，未出界卒。

translations.literal: The Xu army, glad to recover the two prefectures, dared not make trouble; Yin then set out for the capital but died before leaving the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu army, glad to recover the two prefectures, dared not make trouble. Yin then set out for the capital but died before leaving the border.

sentences.zh: 愔在徐州七年，百姓稱理，詔贈右僕射。

translations.literal: Yin was at Xuzhou for seven years; the common people praised his governance. An edict posthumously granted him Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was at Xuzhou for seven years, and the common people praised his governance. An edict posthumously granted him Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 盧群，字載初，范陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Qun—Lu Qun, styled Zaichu, was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qun, styled Zaichu, was a man of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，初學於太安山。

translations.literal: In youth he loved reading and first studied on Mount Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved reading and first studied on Mount Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使陳少遊聞其名，辟為從事。

translations.literal: Huainan Military Commissioner Chen Shaoyou heard of his name and recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan Military Commissioner Chen Shaoyou heard of his name and recruited him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 建中末，薦於朝廷，會李希烈反叛，詔諸將討之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianzhong era he was recommended to the court; it happened that Li Xilie rebelled, and an edict ordered the generals to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianzhong era he was recommended to the court. It happened that Li Xilie rebelled, and an edict ordered the generals to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 以群為監察御史、江西行營糧料使。

translations.literal: Qun was made Supervising Censor and grain commissioner of the Jiangxi expeditionary camp.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was made Supervising Censor and grain commissioner of the Jiangxi expeditionary camp.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，江西節度、嗣曹王臯奏為判官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, Jiangxi Military Commissioner and Heir Prince of Cao Li Gao memorialized appointing him judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan, Jiangxi Military Commissioner and Heir Prince of Cao Li Gao memorialized appointing him judge.

sentences.zh: 曹王移鎮江陵、襄陽，群皆從之，幕府之事，委以咨決，以正直聞。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Cao moved his garrison to Jiangling and Xiangyang, Qun followed him; affairs of the military commission were entrusted to his counsel and decision, and he was known for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Cao moved his garrison to Jiangling and Xiangyang, Qun followed him. Affairs of the military commission were entrusted to his counsel and decision, and he was known for uprightness.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年，入拜侍御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he entered the capital and was appointed Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he entered the capital and was appointed Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 有人誣告故尚父子儀嬖人張氏宅中有寶玉者，張氏兄弟又與尚父家子孫相告訴，詔促按其獄。

translations.literal: Someone falsely accused the late Duke Guo's favorite Zhang's household of possessing precious jade; the Zhang brothers also sued the Duke Guo's sons and grandsons; an edict ordered a hasty investigation of the case.
translations.idiomatic: Someone falsely accused the late Duke Guo's favorite Zhang's household of possessing precious jade. The Zhang brothers also sued the Duke Guo's sons and grandsons. An edict ordered a hasty investigation of the case.

sentences.zh: 群奏曰：「張氏以子儀在時分財，子弟不合爭奪。

translations.literal: Qun memorialized: "The Zhang household divided property while Ziyi was alive; the sons and nephews should not contend and seize.
translations.idiomatic: Qun memorialized, "The Zhang household divided property while Ziyi was alive; the sons and nephews should not contend and seize.

sentences.zh: 然張氏宅與子儀親仁宅，皆子儀家事。

translations.literal: Yet the Zhang household residence and Ziyi's Qinren residence are both household affairs of Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Zhang household residence and Ziyi's Qinren residence are both household affairs of Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 子儀有大勛，伏望陛下特赦而勿問，俾私自引退。」

translations.literal: Ziyi had great merit; I hope Your Majesty will specially pardon and not inquire, allowing them to withdraw privately."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi had great merit. I hope Your Majesty will specially pardon and not inquire, allowing them to withdraw privately."

sentences.zh: 德宗從其言，時人嘉其識大體。

translations.literal: Dezong followed his words; contemporaries praised his grasp of the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong followed his words, and contemporaries praised his grasp of the larger pattern.

sentences.zh: 累轉左司、職方、兵部三員外郎中。

translations.literal: He was successively transferred through three outside director posts: Left Department, Bureau of Appointments, and Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively transferred through three outside director posts: Left Department, Bureau of Appointments, and Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 淮西節度使吳少誠擅開決司、洧等水漕輓溉田，遣中使止之，少誠不奉詔。

translations.literal: Huaiwest Military Commissioner Wu Shaocheng unilaterally opened the Si, Wei, and other waterways for canal transport and irrigation of fields; the court sent a palace envoy to stop him, but Shaocheng did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwest Military Commissioner Wu Shaocheng unilaterally opened the Si, Wei, and other waterways for canal transport and irrigation of fields. The court sent a palace envoy to stop him, but Shaocheng did not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 令群使蔡州詰之，少誠曰：「開大渠，大利於人。」

translations.literal: The court ordered Qun to go to Caizhou to interrogate him; Shaocheng said: "Opening the great canal greatly benefits the people."
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Qun to go to Caizhou to interrogate him. Shaocheng said, "Opening the great canal greatly benefits the people."

sentences.zh: 群曰：「為臣之道，不合自專，雖便於人，須俟君命。

translations.literal: Qun said: "The way of a subject does not permit self-willed action; even if it benefits the people, one must await the ruler's command.
translations.idiomatic: Qun said, "The way of a subject does not permit self-willed action. Even if it benefits the people, one must await the ruler's command.

sentences.zh: 且人臣須以恭恪為事，若事君不盡恭恪，即責下吏恭恪，固亦難矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover a subject must take reverent respect as his service; if one does not serve the ruler with full reverent respect, then demanding reverent respect from subordinate officials is also difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover a subject must take reverent respect as his service. If one does not serve the ruler with full reverent respect, then demanding reverent respect from subordinate officials is also difficult."

sentences.zh: 凡數百千言，諭以君臣之分，忠順之義，少誠乃從命，即停工役。

translations.literal: Altogether several hundred to a thousand words, he instructed him on the division between ruler and subject and the meaning of loyalty and obedience; Shaocheng then obeyed the order and immediately halted the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether several hundred to a thousand words, he instructed him on the division between ruler and subject and the meaning of loyalty and obedience. Shaocheng then obeyed the order and immediately halted the labor.

sentences.zh: 群博涉，有口辨，好談論，與少誠言古今成敗之事，無不聳聽。

translations.literal: Qun was broadly learned, eloquent, and loved discourse; when he spoke with Shaocheng of success and failure in ancient and modern times, none failed to listen with rapt attention.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was broadly learned, eloquent, and loved discourse. When he spoke with Shaocheng of success and failure in ancient and modern times, none failed to listen with rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 又與唱和賦詩，自言以反側，常蒙隔在恩外，群於筵中醉而歌曰：「祥瑞不在鳳凰、麒麟，太平須得邊將、忠臣。

translations.literal: They also exchanged poems in singing harmony; Shaocheng said that as a rebel he was often kept outside imperial grace; at the banquet Qun, drunk, sang: "Auspicious omens are not in phoenix and qilin; great peace must have frontier generals and loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They also exchanged poems in singing harmony. Shaocheng said that as a rebel he was often kept outside imperial grace. At the banquet Qun, drunk, sang: "Auspicious omens are not in phoenix and qilin; great peace must have frontier generals and loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 衛、霍真誠奉主，貔虎十萬一身。

translations.literal: Wei and Huo sincerely serve their lord; tiger and leopard, a hundred thousand in one body.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Huo sincerely serve their lord; tiger and leopard, a hundred thousand in one body.

sentences.zh: 江、河潛註息浪，蠻貊款塞無塵。

translations.literal: Rivers and streams pour in secret, waves subside; barbarians sincerely come to the border, dustless.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and streams pour in secret, waves subside; barbarians sincerely come to the border, dustless.

sentences.zh: 但得百僚師長肝膽，不用三軍羅綺金銀。」

translations.literal: Only need the hundred officials and commanders with liver and gall; need not the three armies with silk brocade, gold, and silver."
translations.idiomatic: Only need the hundred officials and commanders with liver and gall; need not the three armies with silk brocade, gold, and silver."

sentences.zh: 少誠大感悅。

translations.literal: Shaocheng was greatly moved and delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng was greatly moved and delighted.

sentences.zh: 群以奉使稱旨，俄遷檢校秘書監，兼御史中丞、義成軍節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Because Qun's mission pleased the emperor, he was soon promoted to Honorary Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and expeditionary army marshal of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qun's mission pleased the emperor, he was soon promoted to Honorary Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and expeditionary army marshal of the Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 貞元十六年四月，節度姚南仲歸朝，拜群義成軍節度、鄭滑觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan, when Military Commissioner Yao Nanzhong returned to court, Qun was appointed Military Commissioner of the Yicheng Army and Commissioner of Zheng and Hua observation, among other duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan, when Military Commissioner Yao Nanzhong returned to court, Qun was appointed Military Commissioner of the Yicheng Army and Commissioner of Zheng and Hua observation, among other duties.

sentences.zh: 先寓居鄭州，典質良田數頃；

translations.literal: Earlier he had lived at Zhengzhou and pawned several qing of fine land;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had lived at Zhengzhou and pawned several qing of fine land;

sentences.zh: 及為節度使至鎮，各與本地契書，分付所管令長，令召還本主，時論稱美。

translations.literal: when he became military commissioner and reached his post, he gave the contracts to each local magistrate under his jurisdiction and ordered them recalled to the original owners; contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: when he became military commissioner and reached his post, he gave the contracts to each local magistrate under his jurisdiction and ordered them recalled to the original owners. Contemporary opinion praised this.

sentences.zh: 尋遇疾，其年十月卒，時年五十九，廢朝一日，贈工部尚書，赗賻布帛、米粟有差。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill; in the tenth month of that year he died at the age of fifty-nine. Court mourning was suspended for one day; he was posthumously granted Minister of Works, with differentiated funeral gifts of cloth, silk, grain, and rice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill. In the tenth month of that year he died at the age of fifty-nine. Court mourning was suspended for one day. He was posthumously granted Minister of Works, with differentiated funeral gifts of cloth, silk, grain, and rice.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：韋南康、張徐州，慷慨下位之中，橫身喪亂之際，力扶衰運，氣激壯圖，義風凜凜，聳動群醜，舂盜之喉，折賊之角，可謂忠矣！

translations.literal: The historian comments: Wei of Nankang and Zhang of Xuzhou, from generous stations in low rank amid calamity and disorder, threw themselves into supporting a declining age; their spirit stirred bold designs, their righteous bearing awe-inspiring, moving the crowd of villains—choking the throats of robbers, breaking the horns of rebels—can be called loyal!
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Wei of Nankang and Zhang of Xuzhou, from generous stations in low rank amid calamity and disorder, threw themselves into supporting a declining age. Their spirit stirred bold designs, their righteous bearing awe-inspiring, moving the crowd of villains—choking the throats of robbers, breaking the horns of rebels—can be called loyal!

sentences.zh: 而韋公季年，惑賊辟之奸說，欲兼巴、益，則誌未可量。

translations.literal: Yet in his later years Duke Wei was misled by a rebel's treacherous counsel and wished to annex Ba and Yi—then his ambition cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his later years Duke Wei was misled by a rebel's treacherous counsel and wished to annex Ba and Yi—then his ambition cannot be measured.

sentences.zh: 徐州請覲，頗有規諫之言，所謂以道匡君，能以功名始終者。

translations.literal: At his court audience the man of Xuzhou offered much admonishing speech—what is called using the Way to correct the ruler, able to begin and end with merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: At his court audience the man of Xuzhou offered much admonishing speech—what is called using the Way to correct the ruler, able to begin and end with merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 盧載初喻少誠，還地券，君子哉！

translations.literal: Lu Zaichu instructing Shaocheng and returning land contracts—a gentleman indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zaichu instructing Shaocheng and returning land contracts—a gentleman indeed!

sentences.zh: 三子之賢，不可多得。

translations.literal: The worth of these three men is not easily found in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: The worth of these three men is not easily found in abundance.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：南康英壯，力匡交喪。

translations.literal: In praise it is said: The heroic and stalwart Prince of Nankang, with his strength rectified the collapse of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: The heroic Prince of Nankang, who with his strength steadied the realm in its time of collapse.

sentences.zh: 張侯義烈，誌平亂象。

translations.literal: Marquis Zhang, righteous and fierce, whose resolve was to pacify the omens of chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zhang, righteous and fierce, resolved to pacify the signs of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 見危能振，蹈利無謗。

translations.literal: Seeing peril they could rouse themselves; treading profit without slander.
translations.idiomatic: They roused themselves when peril appeared and walked among profit without reproach.

sentences.zh: 韋德不周，張心可亮。

translations.literal: Wei's virtue was not complete; Zhang's heart may be made bright.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's virtue fell short of perfection; Zhang's heart shines clear.
